  content = '## Love and Thunder

Taika Waititi returned to direct Thor''s fourth solo film, bringing even more comedy and color. Christian Bale delivered a genuinely terrifying performance as Gorr the God Butcher, while Natalie Portman returned as Jane Foster wielding Mjolnir as the Mighty Thor. The film divided audiences between those who loved the comedy and those who wanted more dramatic weight.

## The Legacy

- **Christian Bale** — Delivered a haunting villain performance that many felt deserved more screen time
- **Mighty Thor** — Natalie Portman returned after a decade to wield Mjolnir as Jane Foster
- **Love Daughter** — Thor adopted Love (India Hemsworth), Gorr''s resurrected daughter
- **Zeus and Olympus** — Introduced the Greek gods and Hercules (Brett Goldstein) in the post-credits
- **Divisive Comedy** — The film''s heavy comedy tone split the fanbase

## Fun Facts

- Christian Bale was unrecognizable under Gorr''s makeup and prosthetics
- Chris Hemsworth''s real daughter India played Love, Gorr''s daughter
- Russell Crowe improvised much of his Zeus performance with an exaggerated Greek accent
- The screaming goats became a viral meme and were based on a real internet video
- Natalie Portman trained extensively for the physical demands of playing Mighty Thor

## Viewing Context

Love and Thunder follows **Thor: Ragnarok** and **Avengers: Endgame** directly. It opens with the Guardians of the Galaxy before Thor goes solo. Jane Foster''s cancer storyline is adapted from Jason Aaron''s acclaimed comic run. The post-credits scene introduces Hercules (Brett Goldstein) as a future antagonist.',
